# Start here

The maintained annex is `technical-annex-v2/` in the **SC14_JM** repository.
Open `output/technical-annex.html`, `.pdf` or `.docx`. Edit the plain-text
files in `report/` and rebuild from this folder:

```sh
Rscript build.R           # annex and this guide in HTML
Rscript build.R all       # HTML, PDF and Word
Rscript build.R pdf annex # one document and format
Rscript build.R check     # verify inputs and risk calculations
```

The build uses R and Quarto. PDF also needs XeLaTeX and the fonts in
`report/_quarto.yml`. Installation commands are in `README.md`. The supplied
`software/jjmR_1.2020.1.tar.gz` preserves the local package fixes used by the
annex. The build records package versions, logs and product hashes in `validation/`.

These are the saved September 2026 Model 1.06 working results. This migration
changes the workflow and location; assessment findings and decision status remain
as recorded in the annex. Running the build reads saved fits, calculates summaries
and draws figures. A new assessment or projection requires a separate JJM run.

# Follow the calculation

| Source | R calculation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `data/assessment/config/`, `input/`, `results/` | `R/prepare_report.R` reads four fits with `jjmR::readJJM` | Model objects, status and catch summaries in `data/derived/` |
| Base `msy_mt` block | Mean of column 10 for 2017–2026 | Fixed BMSY for stock status and risk |
| `data/projections/*_R.rep` | `R/risk_data.R` reads projected SSB and ADMB standard error | All 180 annual records in `data/derived/risk-data.csv` |
| Saved fits and retrospectives | R chunks in `report/annex_tables.qmd` and `annex_plots.qmd` | Report tables and figures |
| Text, tables and figures | Quarto assembles the includes in `report/technical-annex.qmd` | HTML, PDF and Word in `output/` |

## Example probability

For each stock, scenario and year, `R/risk_data.R` calculates:

```r
100 * pnorm(BMSY, mean = projected_SSB, sd = ADMB_SE,
            lower.tail = FALSE)
```

The fixed target uses the **base** assessment; the projected biomass and standard
error use the **.ls** ten-year projection. All quantities are in kt. The result is
an annual conditional normal probability. The calculation holds BMSY fixed and
excludes uncertainty in that threshold. R recalculates every record and compares
it with the reviewed export before the report uses it.

For single-stock scenario 4 in 2028, the target is 6,869.029 kt, projected SSB is
5,774.3 kt and its standard error is 1,147.25 kt. The result is 16.999%, displayed
as **17%**. The tables show 2028, 2031 and 2036: two, five and ten years after 2026.

## Keep the reference points distinct

The fixed risk target is a **2017–2026 mean of annual base BMSY**. The model's
separate **global scalar BMSY** uses 2011–2025 mean selectivity. Scenario 4
optimizes and applies its projection FMSY with 2023–2025 mean future selectivity.
The equations and scalar values are in `report/annex_reference_points.qmd`;
`data/projections/manifest.json` identifies the saved projection run and template.

The original five-year projection plots remain historical comparisons. The risk
tables use the separate ten-year products. Three explanatory diagrams and the
reference-value tables retain reviewed September values; inspect their labels
when changing models. Original diagram drawing scripts are preserved in the
archive. These saved elements require an explicit update when new runs are adopted.

# Make a change

For prose, edit `report/annex_text.qmd` or the relevant included section. For
literature, edit `report/refs.bib`. Keep figure and table labels stable. After a
Word review, transfer agreed edits back into the `.qmd` source and rebuild.

For a new assessment, complete and review the model run first. The optional R
helper copies this release's explicit set of 24 assessment files into a **new**
folder and checks that the fits and saved objects can be read:

```sh
Rscript R/snapshot_assessment.R /path/to/jjm /path/to/new-snapshot
```

Review that candidate before replacing `data/assessment/`. A new model or year
requires reviewing the helper's selection, year/model settings, recruitment
periods, retrospective years, reference values and projection horizons. Update
the ten-year run products and their uncertainty calculation separately. Record
the source revision and changes, then update `data/input-checksums.csv` only for
the reviewed inputs. The inventory is deliberately checked rather than rewritten
by a routine build.

# Check and hand over

Run `Rscript build.R check`, rebuild the required formats, and inspect status,
reference and risk tables, figure captions and links. Build logs are in
`validation/logs/`. `validation/build.csv` records each product's date and hash;
`validation/R-session.txt` records the build environment. The migration check
records what was compared with the previous package. Rendering and automated
checks provide only part of accessibility validation; reading order and assistive
technology still require review.

Keep the whole `technical-annex-v2/` folder together. Its data links are relative,
and the build needs no other local checkout. Historical sources and concise
reviews are isolated in `archive/september-12-history.zip`. The parent repository's
wiki has a separate build; it is independent of the annex's R workflow. Commit
reviewed source and generated reports together when ready, and treat publication
as a separate step.
